column11: This is the engine acceleration filter, and it is the twin of CM848 0x38760. It computes ESESAC (0x80a292) = the measured speed ESCMES (0x80ccf4) minus the previous pass's speed (0x800048), then stores the speed as the new previous. ESFT01AC (0x80a294) = cm550_signedFirstOrderFilter(ESESAC, &engine_acceleration_first_stage_filter_state); a value below ESFT01MN (0x807a48) or above ESFT01MX (0x807a46) is clamped and the accumulator is reset to the clamp. ESFT02AC (0x80a296) = the second-stage filter of the first stage. CM848 does the same steps in the same order with the same calibration layout: coefficients at 0x408808 / 0x40880a then max 0x40880c and min 0x40880e, against 0x807a42 / 0x807a44 / 0x807a46 / 0x807a48 here. The one difference is the offset-binary accumulator of CM550's signed filter (subi.l #0x80000000 after the << 16). Twin rule used throughout this output: representation-only differences (offset binary, lookup-descriptor pointers) keep a twin, as initializeHighSpeedGovernorGainSet already does; a real extra or missing step or a different constant makes a counterpart. Run every pass by vp44_engine_management_system right after the engine speed calculation, as CM848 runs it in hpcr_periodicTaskSet_fuelFinal after cm848_updateEngineSpeedFromCrankSignal. Nothing in it is output control or timing.

The twin of CM550 0xb210 (see that row), so the two take one shared unprefixed name. Both compute the speed change since the last pass and run two first-order filter stages, with the first stage clamped to its minimum / maximum and its accumulator reset to the clamp. The steps, their order, the calibration layout and the position in the periodic task are the same. The only difference is CM550's offset-binary accumulator.

Start-up initializer of the two engine acceleration filter records and the previous speed. It sets engine_acceleration_first_stage_filter_state.accumulator = 0x80000000 (0 in the offset binary of cm550_signedFirstOrderFilter) and .coefficient = &engine_acceleration_first_stage_filter_coefficient (0x807a42, ESFT01TC). The second stage gets the same (0x807a44, ESFT02TC), and the previous engine speed 0x800048 is set to 0. That is all it does; there is no DMA. It is the twin of CM848 0x38824: the same five stores in the same order (accumulator 0, coefficients 0x408808 / 0x40880a, previous speed 0x3fb3ae = 0), and both are called once by the application main.

The twin of CM550 0xb5e4 (see that row): the same five stores in the same order. It clears both engine acceleration filter accumulators, points their coefficients at engine_acceleration_first_stage_filter_coefficient / _second_stage_filter_coefficient and clears engine_acceleration_engine_speed_previous. It gets one shared name, which also replaces the banned 'init'.

This is the whole low speed governor (LSG). It first computes the throttle deadband reference offset = cm550_exponentialMovingAverage(0x80825a x validated throttle, &low_speed_governor_throttle_reference_offset_filter_state). LSRF lsg_breakpoint_speed is the operator or the datalink breakpoint, and LSAJRFES (the reference adjusted with throttle position) is clamped. The governor runs while FSGVFLST (0x80a8f2) is 11 (the LSG fueling state), or while LSEXFL (0x80daf6) says the LSG is running and the speed is within reference + offset. Each pass computes the speed error x gain >> 9 and passes it through low_speed_governor_error_filter (cm550_signedFirstOrderFilter), clamped to LSFTMX / LSFTMN with the accumulator reset. On the first pass the filter accumulator is preset in offset binary. Then come the integrator reset, the P / I / D terms, the LSG fueling clamps and lsg_fuel_output_clamped, which goes to lsg_governor_fuel_demand in state 11 (the integrator preset vp44_FUN_00025a34 runs on entry to state 11). It touches neither VP44 nor timing, so the prefix is cm550_ (generic). It is a counterpart, not a twin, of CM848's LSG. CM848 splits the work into cm848_calculateLowSpeedGovernorErrorTerms (0x28ba4) and cm848_runLowSpeedGovernor (0x27ff8) and adds jerk terms, gain adjustments, the alternator load fuel and a reset delay.

Start-up initializer of the low speed governor. It points low_speed_governor_throttle_reference_offset_filter_state.coefficient at 0x808258 (e2m 1064 +22 LSDEFTTC, the throttle deadband fix filter constant) and low_speed_governor_error_filter.coefficient at 0x80823e (1064 +8 LSFTTC). It then runs cm550_epsControlModeInit (0x26308, the LSG gain-set selection reset: gain set 0, default P / I / D gains copied into the override set) and sets LSMXLMFL lsg_fueling_clamp_max_0_100 (0x80dae8) = 0x1700. It sets no accumulator: the LSG presets the error filter when it starts. Its CM848 counterparts are cm848_initializeLowSpeedGovernorParameters (0x28618: gain selection init, three gain adjustments, clamp maximum 0x1700, the alternator load filter) and cm848_setGovernorFilterPointer (0x28d30: only the error filter's coefficient pointer). The steps differ, so neither is a twin.

This is the all-speed governor (ASG). It runs only while FSDSFLST (0x80ded4, the user fueling state) is 7, 3, 2 or 30. On a state change it presets the reference from the droop and sets all_speed_governor_reference_filter_state.accumulator = reference << 16. In state 7 it runs cm550_dzgTimingAndPressureControlStateMachine; in the other states it filters the working reference with cm550_exponentialMovingAverage(&all_speed_governor_reference_filter_state) and keeps coefficient >> 2. It then computes the ASG state terms x1..x6, the reset states, the derivative deadband and the fueling limits into ASMXFL / fuel_demand_selected. The old name is snake_case and does not say which governor. It is a counterpart, not a twin, of CM848 cm848_runOperatingModeSpeedGovernor (0xea00). CM848 runs in states 7 / 2 / 30 / 37, adds the no-load fuel call, the negative reference slew and the deadband compensation, and in state 7 runs cm848_calculateGovernorReferenceSpeedBlend. The decompile shows it called from two task sets, but the ROM has one call site: the records 0x1b572 and 0x1b57e overlap (0x1b572 falls into 0x1b57e).

The power take-off (PTO) reference speed smoothing. It first calls 0x4d988, then, while PTSS (0x80dc26) is 1: if |PTDSRF (0x80dc24) - PTRFRP (0x80dc18)| <= PTRFLM (0x8088aa), PTRFRP = PTDSRF. Otherwise it sets the reference filter's accumulator = PTRFRP << 16, filters cm550_exponentialMovingAverage(PTDSRF, &power_take_off_reference_filter_state) and moves PTRFRP toward the result by at least PTRFLM. CM848 0x2ac44 does the same compares (bhi / blt / ble against bgt / bge / ble) and stores in the same order with the same layout: requested speed and active flag adjacent (0x80dc24 / 26 against 0x40af4c / 4e), step and coefficient adjacent (0x8088aa / ac against 0x40719e / a0). Both sit in the same task position: before the PTO governor run and the PTO-or-user fueling selection (CM550 0x2d3c6 then 0x2dcb0, which is misnamed cm550_oil_pressure_shutdown_controller; CM848 cm848_runPowerTakeOffGovernor then cm848_selectPowerTakeOffOrUserFueling). The gap is the first step: 0x4d988 lies in the undumped ROM above 0x40000, so its body cannot be compared with CM848's cm848_rampPowerTakeOffReferenceEngineSpeed (0x2ba7c) at the same place. It fits: PTDSRF has no writer in the dumped ROM. Hence medium confidence for the twin claim. Of the decompile's two call sites, ROM 0x1b58a is the only instruction (overlapping records 0x1b572 / 0x1b57e).

The twin of CM550 0x2dbde (see that row), so it drops the cm848_ prefix for the shared name. Every step after the first call matches in order and layout. The first callee cannot be compared (CM550's 0x4d988 is undumped), hence medium.

Start-up initializer of the PTO governor. power_take_off_speed_error_filter.accumulator = 0x80000000 (offset-binary 0) and .coefficient = 0x80889a (10AA +2 PTFTTC 'PD GOVERNOR ERROR FILTER CONSTANT'). Then the reference filter initializer 0x2dc9e runs and PTAJDG / PTAJIG / PTAJPG (0x80dc1e / 20 / 22, the D / I / P gain adjustments) are set to 0x80. Last, the four lookup descriptor sizes are set to 2 (0x801c1c, 0x801c2a, 0x801c38, then 0x801c0e) together with their axis / value pointers. CM848 0x2abc8 does the same in the same order: error filter accumulator 0 and coefficient 0x407190, bl 0x2ad48, 0x80 to 0x40af44 / 46 / 48 (QD / QI / QP), then the caches 0x3fafc6 / c8 / ca and last 0x3fafc4. In both, the lowest address comes last. The only differences are representation: the offset binary and the pointer loads of CM550's lookup descriptors, which initializeHighSpeedGovernorGainSet also shares a name across. Both parents run three initializers in the same order: cm550_initMultiSystemParameters (0x345c8: 0xd59e, 0x258d6, 0x2db2a) and cm848_dispatchModeHandlers (0x42978: 0x10248, 0x50db88, 0x2abc8). So this is a twin.
The twin of CM550 0x2db2a (see that row): it takes the same shared name without the cm848_ prefix. Both have the same stores in the same order and are the third call of their three-call parent.

It sets power_take_off_reference_filter_state.accumulator = 0 and then .coefficient = 0x8088ac (10AA +14 PTRFRMTC 'REFERENCE SPEED CHANGE CONST.'), and does nothing else. Its one caller is the PTO governor initializer 0x2db2a. CM848 0x2ad48 is identical (accumulator 0x3fafd0 = 0, then coefficient 0x3fafcc = 0x4071a0) and is called only by 0x2abc8, so this is a twin.
The twin of CM550 0x2dc9e: identical code (accumulator 0, then the coefficient pointer) and the same caller role, so they share one unprefixed name.

(Extra: not in the task list. It is the third user of power_take_off_reference_filter_state.) It sets PTRFRP (0x80dc18, the smoothed PTO reference) = ENGRPM (0x80ccf6, the filtered engine speed) and clears power_take_off_reference_filter_state.accumulator. Its one caller is the PTO engagement preset 0x2d9d2. CM848 0x2ad28 is identical: power_take_off_governor_smoothed_reference_engine_speed = engine_speed_state.filtered_engine_speed (0x40b7ba), accumulator 0x3fafd0 = 0. Its one caller is cm848_presetPowerTakeOffGovernorOnEngagement, so this is a twin. It captures no rpm snapshot apart from that reference.
The twin of CM550 0x2dc8c (identical two stores, the same caller role), so it takes the shared unprefixed name.

Deletion preferred: this is not a separate function. The proposed name is only a gate-valid fallback in case the row is kept. 0x1ae0c is the last three instructions of cm550_FUN_0001ade8: 0x1ade8 runs straight through 0x1ae06 and 0x1ae0c to the rts at 0x1ae20, with no prologue at either inner address. What it sets up is engine_deceleration_rate_filter_state (accumulator 0x80000000, coefficient 0x807f66), and that is all. The dumped ROM has no reference to it (references_to.py: 0), and the row came from the J90280.05 relocation map (0x032b00 sensorHistoryTablePointerInit -> 0x01ae0c, 'similar', 64). ROM above 0x40000 is undumped, so a call from there cannot be ruled out, hence medium. To delete: remove the function_renames.csv row and add to deleted_functions.csv '0x0001ae0c,not a function entry: the tail of cm550_FUN_0001ade8 (its engine_deceleration_rate_filter_state set-up after the clears); no reference in the dumped ROM (references_to.py) - the row came from the J90280.05 relocation map (was cm550_sensorHistoryTablePointerInit; PR #53 round 88)'. That is round 85's form for 0x15e06 / 0x28508.

Deletion preferred: this is not a separate function. The proposed name is a fallback in case the row is kept. 0x1ae06 lies inside cm550_FUN_0001ade8: it clears SPTU (0x80d2b4, the ESP tau, misnamed can_transmit_buffer_ptr) and falls into the engine_deceleration_rate_filter_state set-up at 0x1ae0c. That is all it does, and nothing about oil pressure. The dumped ROM has no reference to it (references_to.py: 0), and the row came from the J90280.05 relocation map (0x016af2 initOilPressureModeSystem -> 0x01ae06, 'similar', 78). ROM above 0x40000 is undumped, hence medium. To delete: remove the function_renames.csv row and add to deleted_functions.csv '0x0001ae06,not a function entry: a fall-through point inside cm550_FUN_0001ade8 (the clear of SPTU before the deceleration rate filter set-up); no reference in the dumped ROM (references_to.py) - the row came from the J90280.05 relocation map (was cm550_initOilPressureModeSystem; PR #53 round 88)'.

Start-up initializer of Electronic Smart Power (ESP), e2m blocks 11DC / 11DD (bases 0x80d2b0 / 0x807f64 from the ROM parameter ID table entries 0x3627c / 0x36284). It clears SPRVTZFG (0x80d2ba), SPHILDFG (0x80d2bc, misnamed can_transmit_length), SPTHTR01 (0x80d2b8), SPESDITR (0x80d2b0), SPTUST (0x80d2b6, the source of the current ESP tau) and SPTU (0x80d2b4, the tau, misnamed can_transmit_buffer_ptr). Then engine_deceleration_rate_filter_state.accumulator = 0x80000000 (offset-binary 0) and .coefficient = 0x807f66 (11DD +2 SPDIFTCS). The ESP tau logic cm550_FUN_0001abb2 runs on this state. It is called once from mc68k_applicationMain. CM848 has no counterpart: electronic_smart_power_tau (0x40a2c4) is only read by calculateAlpha, and a scan of both CM848 images finds no store to it. So the prefix is cm550_.

Start-up initializer of the engine protection (EPF) engine speed derate. It sets engine_protection_speed_limit_filter_state.accumulator = the maximum rated engine speed (0x803f40) << 16 and .coefficient = 0x807f3a (10B5 +4 EPRPFTTC 'MAXIMUM RPM LIMIT FILTER TIME CONSTANT'). EPESLM (0x80d288, 'MAXIMUM RPM ALLOWED DUE TO EPF DERATING') = the rated speed, and EPRPDC (0x80d290, 'DIFFERENCE BETWEEN NO_DERATE_RPM AND MAXIMUM_DERATE_RPM') = the rated speed - EPMXDQRP (0x807f38). That is all it does; it sets no threshold pointers. CM848 0x5087e4 is identical: the same four stores in the same order (accumulator = engine_speed_limit_default_cal << 16, coefficient 0x5c2f2, engine_speed_limit_fault_derate = the default, the span = default - engine_speed_limit_fault_derate_full_severity, e2m EPMXDQRP in both). The layout matches too (EPMXDQRP and the coefficient adjacent: 0x807f38 / 3a against 0x5c2f0 / f2; limit and span 8 bytes apart: 0x80d288 / 90 against 0x40a780 / 88). Both are called by the engine protection initializer after the channel set-up (vp44_engineProtectionSystemInit / hpcr_initializeEngineProtection). So this is a twin with one shared name, keeping CM848's wording. Lead: CM848's record 0x3fbd2e and coefficient 0x5c2f2 are still unnamed type-only rows (e.g. engine_speed_limit_fault_derate_filter_state / _filter_coefficient).
The twin of CM550 0x18f4c: the same four stores, the same order, the same e2m EPMXDQRP and the same caller role. It drops the cm848_ prefix for the shared name.

(Extra: not in the task list. It is the user of engine_protection_speed_limit_filter_state.) Over the 9 engine protection channels (configs 0x807032 + 36n, states 0x80d0dc + 46n, severity records 0x8057c0 + 30n) it takes the rpm severity from cm550_protectionThresholdCalculationHelper(..., 1) for each channel whose flag bits (base 0x71 and 0x1a0) are set, and keeps the largest. Then EPESLM = cm550_exponentialMovingAverage(rated speed - severity x EPRPDC >> 8, &engine_protection_speed_limit_filter_state). It does the same as CM848 0x50860c cm848_calculateFaultDerateEngineSpeedLimit, but over a different channel table and with different flag bit bases (CM848: 0x81 and 0x1a4, i.e. starting four channels later). Under this output's rule (different constants make a counterpart) it is a counterpart, cm550_. If the runHighSpeedGovernorPid precedent (different constants accepted) is preferred, the shared name calculateFaultDerateEngineSpeedLimit fits both, with CM848 0x50860c renamed to it.

It sets pedal_fault_mode_engine_speed_filter_state.accumulator = 0 and then .coefficient = 0x80820e (10CE +0 LHESFTTC, the limp home engine speed filter constant), and does nothing else; there is no fuel demand table. CM848 0x50db88 cm848_initDroopModeStateVariables is identical: accumulator 0x3fcbe0 = 0, then coefficient 0x3fcbdc = 0x5c48e (e2m 10CE +0 Limp_Home_Engine_Speed_Filter_Constant). Both are the second of the three initializers their parent runs (cm550_initMultiSystemParameters at 0x345ce, cm848_dispatchModeHandlers at 0x42988), so this is a twin. The CM848 name is wrong as well, since nothing in it is about droop.

The twin of CM550 0x258d6: the identical two stores (pedal_fault_mode_engine_speed_filter_state accumulator 0, coefficient pedal_fault_mode_engine_speed_filter_coefficient) and the same position in the three-call parent. The shared name also fixes the old one (no droop, no 'init').

(Extra: not in the task list. It is a user of pedal_fault_mode_engine_speed_filter_state.) It is the pedal fault mode preset: fuel_demand_ramped (0x80dab8, the ramp) and fuel_demand_target (0x801a3c, the slewed limit) = current_fuel_demand, and the filter's accumulator = ESCMES (0x80ccf4) << 16. CM848 0x50da7c cm848_presetPedalFaultModeFuelDemand does the same three stores in the same order: ramp 0x40ae6c and limit_previous 0x3fcbe6 = final_fueling, accumulator = engine_speed_state.engine_speed << 16. The layout matches too: the slewed limit sits 10 bytes after the filter record in both (0x801a32 -> 0x801a3c, 0x3fcbdc -> 0x3fcbe6). Both are called only by the mode-6 entry (cm550_FUN_00025806 / cm848_transitionEngineOperatingMode), so this is a twin.
The twin of CM550 0x258b0: the same three stores, the same order, the same layout and the same mode-6 entry caller. It takes the shared unprefixed name.

(Extra: not in the task list. It is the user of pedal_fault_mode_engine_speed_filter_state.) While FSDSFLST (0x80ded4) is 6, the accelerator pedal fault mode, it runs cm550_exponentialMovingAverage(ESCMES, &pedal_fault_mode_engine_speed_filter_state). From that it sets the fuel limit = offset - slope x speed / 0x8b21 (floored at the minimum), slews the target down by the decrease rate, and ramps the fuel demand by the increment while the throttle is off idle (initial value on the first pass, minimum fueling at idle) into fuel_demand_selected. This is a counterpart, not a twin, of CM848 cm848_calculatePedalFaultModeFuelDemandAndSpeedLimit (0x50d864). CM848 has the same core and the same 0x8b21 divisor, but adds the brake-on limits and engine speed limit source 14 with its road speed derate.

(Extra: not in the task list. It is a user of low_speed_governor_error_filter.) It presets the LSG speed error: LSER (0x80dae0) = gain 0x808240 x (LSAJRFES - ENGRPM - offset 0x808264) >> 9, clamped to LSFTMN / LSFTMX. Then low_speed_governor_error_filter.accumulator = that << 16 in offset binary, it runs cm550_epsInitializationWrapper (0x262fa) and stores the speed in 0x801a70 for the derivative. It touches no VP44 and no fuel, so the prefix is cm550_. It is a real entry (after the rts at 0x25ff0, with a movem prologue) but has no reference in the dumped ROM, so its caller is probably in the undumped ROM above 0x40000; hence medium.

Start-up initializer of the alpha state. It sets alpha_fuel_rate_filter_state.accumulator = 0 and .coefficient = 0x807ab0 (e2m 104B +10 APFLFTTC, the alpha fuel rate filter constant). APAPBA, the alpha base (0x80a8fa), the LSG / AFC exit timer active flags (0x80a90e / 0x80a912), 0x80a916 and FSLSSTFG (0x80a908, the semaphore that latches LSG events) are all set to 0. It has no VP44 or control structure. Its counterpart is CM848 0xe748 cm848_initializeAlpha (the filter, alpha_base, the two timer flags, alpha_low_speed_governor_state_detected_flag): the same stores in the same order, except CM550's extra clr.w of 0x80a916 (104A +1E, no other reference in the dumped ROM). By this output's rule a real extra step makes a counterpart, hence cm550_. If the selectHighSpeedGovernorGainSet precedent (a twin despite one extra step) is preferred, the shared name initializeAlpha fits both, with CM848 0xe748 cm848_initializeAlpha -> initializeAlpha. That would match the twin alpha family (calculateAlpha / calculateAlphaBase / calculateAlpha*Result).

Start-up initializer of the engine speed calculation 0x171be, which uses all four of the values it sets. engine_speed_filter_state.accumulator = 0 and .coefficient = 0x807ea8 (100B +0 ESESFTTC 'TIME CONSTANT FOR THE FILTER USED ON THE 2^N PULSE AVERAGE'). The main pulse period timeout working value 0x80d06c (misnamed governor_rpm_target_adjusted) = ESMXTM01 (0x807eaa). The speed sensor selection routine pointer 0x80d08c = 0x1770a, the routine that sets ESSNSE. ESSNSE (0x80cd18, 'SPEED_SENSOR_SELECT') = 0. So it sets up more than the speed source, and 'init' is the banned short form. CM848 does the same filter set-up inside its much larger mpc555_resetEngineTimingAccumulators (0x43ddc), so this is a counterpart with a CM550-only name.

(Extra: not in the task list. It is the user of engine_speed_filter_state.) It is the engine speed calculation, not a fuel limit. It counts down the main / backup / external lost-signal counters, converts the pulse periods to speeds (0x80cd06 / 0x80cd04 / 0x80cd16) and sets the speed-lost and cam / crank sync faults. It calls the speed sensor selection routine through 0x80d08c, and for the selected sensor (ESSNSE) filters the speed into ENGRPM (0x80ccf6) with cm550_exponentialMovingAverage(&engine_speed_filter_state); a lost sensor gives zeros, and an override gives 0x80a92c. Finally it sets not_safe_to_program_flag by the engine state and scales the pulse period timeouts by speed. It runs right before the engine acceleration filter. A counterpart of CM848 cm848_updateEngineSpeedFromCrankSignal (0x44374); it accesses no MC68336 register directly, so the prefix is cm550_.

(Extra: not in the task list. It is the user of power_take_off_speed_error_filter.) It runs the PTO governor while PTSS (0x80dc26) is 1. On the first active pass (previous flag 0x801c0c != 1) it calls the engagement preset 0x2d9d2. It computes the gain adjustment from the smoothed reference (formula or table by PTGM, clamped 0x20c..0x7ccc) and the speed error x gain >> 14 through cm550_signedFirstOrderFilter(&power_take_off_speed_error_filter), clamped. Then come the D / I / P gain adjustment tables, the proportional / derivative / integral terms and the fuel demand output; the output is 0 while inactive. Nothing in it is initialization or protection. The old unprefixed name is a stale shared name: CM848 took it off 0x2a960, its engagement preset, which plays a different role. This is a counterpart of CM848 cm848_runPowerTakeOffGovernor (0x2ab2c), which splits the work into cm848_calculatePowerTakeOffGovernorSpeedError and cm848_runPowerTakeOffGovernorPid and runs only the preset on the first pass, where CM550 also runs the error and PID.

(Extra: not in the task list. It is a user of power_take_off_speed_error_filter.) It presets the PTO governor when it engages. It clears the combined PD term (0x80dc14) and presets the smoothed reference (0x2dc8c). Then power_take_off_speed_error_filter.accumulator = 0x80000000 and the filtered error = 0. It computes the gain adjustment from the reference (PTGM formula or table, capped at 0x7ccc), the integral fueling preset from the current fuel demand, and the fuel demand output = current_fuel_demand. CM848 0x2a960 cm848_presetPowerTakeOffGovernorOnEngagement has the same structure in the same order. The differences are not only representation: CM848 also floors the gain at 0x20c here (CM550 does that only in 0x2d3c6), and the scale constants differ (0x7fff against 0x1d70a3). So this is a counterpart, cm550_.

(Extra: not in the task list. It is the user of engine_deceleration_rate_filter_state.) It is the Electronic Smart Power (ESP) logic and runs while calibration_feature_enable_flags_word_9 bit 0x10 is set. It runs the throttle timer SPTHTR01. SPESDIRT (0x80d2b2), the current engine deceleration rate = cm550_signedFirstOrderFilter(previous ENGRPM - ENGRPM, &engine_deceleration_rate_filter_state), drives the deceleration timer SPESDITR. The tau state machine SPTUST (0x80d2b6) sets SPTU (0x80d2b4, the tau: 0, 0x4000 or the 11DD value) within the coolant and intake manifold temperature inhibits. Last, FLINML (0x80d340, 1053 +2, the 4-D fueling interpolation factor; misnamed timing_alpha_blend_factor) = 0x4000 - SPTU. There is no CM848 counterpart (see the 0x1ade8 row), so the prefix is cm550_.

This is the A/D sensor channel loop; it handles no service and no data length. It walks the 25 sensor_debounce_state_t records (22 bytes each, 0x80a2aa to 0x80a4cf), each with its 24-byte config from 0x806ae2 (e2m 1003 +0 ADIMTPCS, channel 0's filter coefficient). For each channel it runs the sample counter against the config's rate byte (+0x17). With the channel's override bit set (calibration_feature_enable_flags_word_5 / 0x803ca0) the output is the override value 0x80a72e[n]. Otherwise it reads the raw value: the forced value 0x80a760[n] (bits 0x803cc0 / 0x803cc2), or the QADC right-justified result register 0xFFF2B0 + 2 x the config's channel index. Then come the high / low range debounce and fault bits, the linearization lookup through the descriptor at 0x80a792 + 14n, and cm550_exponentialMovingAverage(&channel_record->filter) into filtered_value (the config default while the fault is set). The prefix is mc68k_ because it reads the MC68336 QADC result registers (RJURR, $YFF2B0) directly. It is a counterpart, not a twin, of CM848's cm848_processUnsignedSensorChannel (0x5012dc), which is called once per channel with 13 parameters and has no loop. When applying: local_variables.csv:18 is keyed '0x0000b7bc,validateServiceDataLength,filter_state,channel_record'; change its function name with the rename.

Start-up set-up of the A/D channel loop. It writes the 25 linearization lookup descriptors (size 2 plus axis and value pointers at 0x80a792 + 14n). For each channel record it sets the filter (accumulator 0, coefficient = its config record 0x806ae2 + 24n), sets the sample counter to the config's rate so that the first pass samples, and sets the debounce counter / fault flag from the confirmed fault bits. It then runs the loop once (0xb7bc), presets every filter accumulator to the first lookup result << 16 and the filtered value to that result, clears the sample counters and sets the debounce counters from the fault state.
